newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope to visit Lebanon May 10-11 Vatican says.
newsitem.headline: Pope to visit Lebanon May 10-11 Vatican says.

text.p: Pope John Paul will make his long-awaited visit to Lebanon on May 10-11, the Vatican said on Monday.

The Pope had to cancel a visit in May 1994 after the bombing of a Maronite church north of Beirut killed 11 worshippers and injured 59. The Vatican announced the date of the trip after the Pope received Lebanon's Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
Chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said the Pope would stay in the Lebanese capital Beirut during the two-day, weekend visit.
The official reason for the trip is for the Pope to preside at the ceremonial close of a synod of the Lebanese Church, which was held at the Vatican in 1995.
During the trip the Pope is expected to express his support for a comprehensive Middle East peace.
The 76-year-old Pope is also due to visit Sarajevo on April 13 and will make a 10-day trip to his native Poland at the beginning of June. His is also due to visit Prague, Paris and Brazil this year.
